resources.string: Something went wrong in the app. Try again; if it keeps happening, let us know.
Wrong username or password. They\'re the ones you use for LuCI (usually root).
The session with the router ended. Sign in again.
The connection to the router dropped in the middle of the change, so it wasn\'t applied. Try again.
The router doesn\'t allow this for the user you signed in with. Sign in again as root.
The router replied with something the app doesn\'t understand. Check that the address is an OpenWrt router with LuCI; if it is, its version may not be supported yet.
This router lacks a feature the app needs for this. Update OpenWrt or install the full LuCI.
The router didn\'t find what the app was looking for: someone may have changed it in LuCI. Try again.
The router took too long to reply. Try again in a moment.
The router has an internal problem (one of its services isn\'t responding). Restart it and try again.
The router rejected the app\'s request. Try again; if it keeps happening, it\'s a bug in the app: let us know.
LuCI isn\'t available at that address. Is it an OpenWrt router with LuCI installed?
The router returned an internal error. Wait a bit and try again; if it keeps happening, restart it.
No router found with that name. Enter its IP address (for example, 192.168.1.1).
There\'s no way to reach the router from this network. Connect to your home Wi-Fi or turn on remote access.
The router doesn\'t accept connections at that address: either it isn\'t the router, or its web interface (LuCI) is off. Check the address (it\'s usually 192.168.1.1).
Couldn\'t open a secure connection to the router. Try http:// instead of https://.
The router isn\'t responding. Check that you\'re on your home network (or that remote access is on) and that the address is the router\'s.
The connection to the router dropped. Try again.
Couldn\'t talk to the router. Check the connection and try again.
Can\'t reach the router. Android\'s local network permission is missing, and without it the app can\'t see the router at home: grant it in the app settings (Permissions → Nearby devices).
